turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Obs are done before you go in. Blood pressure is 118 over 76, pulse 88, temperature 36.6. She was tearful in the waiting room but she kept saying she's grand.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Come on in, the both of you. It's six weeks from the delivery, isn't it?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Six weeks yesterday. I'm grand, doctor, himself is just fussing. The car park was a nightmare, I nearly turned around.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's not grand. I'm worried sick. She's crying, she's hardly eating, and she's awake even when the baby is flat out asleep.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Ah stop. I do eat. I had toast this morning, newborns wreck everybody.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll hear him in a second. What would you say brought you in?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): I can't sleep even when she sleeps. I'm just lying there, wide awake. It's nothing, though, it'll go.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Can't sleep even when the baby is sleeping. Do you know when that started?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm. I can't put a date on it. Sometime after we got home. A few weeks, maybe.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): The nurse saw you tearful. Are you weepy at home?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): A bit, in the evenings mostly. Not really through the day. I'm not falling apart or anything.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It isn't only evenings. She was crying over the kettle this morning, and she didn't eat the breakfast. One bite of toast.
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): It was more than a bite. I am eating. He's exaggerating the whole thing.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me say that back. Six weeks on, you can't sleep when the baby sleeps, you're weepy in the evenings, and the two of you don't agree on the eating.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, that's the size of it. Sure it'll settle. Mad rain out there today, isn't it?
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): I have to ask this straight. Any thoughts of harming yourself, or of harming the baby?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Never. God no, I'd never hurt her, I just get overwhelmed sometimes.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever, headache, or chest pain?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Not really. None of that.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are the breasts painful, or red?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Not painful. Just a bit full before she feeds, then they're grand.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's asthma on your old notes. Is that still with you?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, mild, since I was a teenager. I only bother with the blue inhaler now.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): The salbutamol. How much are you taking?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Two puffs when I need it. Err, twice a week, maybe three. Not every day.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the brown preventer, were you on that?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Beclamethasone. I stopped it after she was born. I was doing two puffs twice a day, uh no, one puff twice a day. I was grand off it.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze or chest tightness from the asthma lately?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Not that either.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not at night, when you're lying awake?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes. A wee bit wheezy in the bed. Not every night.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): So that's a bit of wheeze some nights, not every night. Any cough?
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): No cough.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): How are the waterworks, all right?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Grand, yeah. No pain or anything.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the bowels?
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): A bit sluggish. Not painful though.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any bleeding still?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): Not really. Just a bit of spotting some days.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood tests in the pregnancy that they flagged?
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): They said the thyroid one at the hospital was borderline. I never got a number. They weren't bothered.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll keep that as borderline, not a confirmed figure. Any allergies to medicines or foods?
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing.
[SEG0044] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm on sertraline myself, fifty milligrams, for my nerves. That's not hers. She won't take a tablet for love nor money.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's your medicine, not hers, I'll not mix them up. Do you smoke, or take a drink?
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): Never smoked. I don't drink now, not with the baby. My mam had awful baby blues with me, she rings every day giving out that I should be resting.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): Who's in the house with you?
[SEG0048] person_3 (PATIENT): Himself and the baby. Mam is only down the road.

[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll have a listen to your chest and a quick look. Chest is clear, no wheeze just now. You look tearful, though you're following me grand. The perineal stitches look healed, no redness.

[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): This is six weeks, not a couple of days of baby blues. My working impression is a postnatal depression, though I can't rule out the thyroid playing a part with that borderline test. I'm not calling it definite today.

[SEG0051] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll arrange bloods today, a thyroid test and a full blood count, and a referral to perinatal mental health for support. No new tablet from me today. Come back and see me in one week. If you feel any urge to harm yourself or the baby before then, don't wait, go to A&E or ring us straight away.
[SEG0052] person_1 (NURSE): I'll book the bloods at the desk now, and your appointment for next week. You did right coming in.

spec.situation: Mother six weeks after delivery, tearful, not sleeping even when the baby sleeps; partner present and anxious; denies harming herself or the baby when asked directly; support and follow-up planned.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
